Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Stimulus-withdrawal time course with AP-1 and chromatin readouts
ideas.description: Like the wreck that outlasts its king, test whether AP-1's imprint outlasts its trigger: pulse cells with a stimulus (e.g., TPA or growth factor), withdraw it, and track AP-1 occupancy (CUT&RUN for Fos/Jun), ATAC-seq, and H3K27ac at target enhancers over days. Memory requires these marks to persist after AP-1 protein and mRNA return to baseline.

ideas.title: Inducible AP-1 degradation during the memory window
ideas.description: Use an auxin-inducible degron tag on endogenous c-Fos or c-Jun to remove AP-1 protein at defined times after a priming stimulus, then re-challenge. If AP-1 is the memory mechanism, degrading it after priming should abolish the faster, stronger secondary response, while degradation before priming should not.

ideas.title: Re-stimulation kinetics as a memory readout
ideas.description: Define memory operationally as a primed-versus-naive difference in the second response: compare the latency, amplitude, and duration of AP-1 target gene induction (single-cell RNA-seq or smFISH) after a rest period. Repeat with AP-1 binding-site mutants at primed enhancers to see whether the faster reactivation depends on AP-1 motifs specifically.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage tracking of heritable AP-1 states
ideas.description: Combine a live AP-1 reporter (e.g., a Fos-promoter destabilized fluorophore or a Fos-TetOff-to-Cre lineage recorder) with time-lapse imaging to follow cell fate across several divisions. Heritable, bimodal persistence of the reporter after the stimulus is gone would show a self-maintaining state rather than a transient response.

ideas.title: Mutate AP-1 sites at persistent enhancers and model the feedback loop
ideas.description: Use CRISPR to mutate AP-1 motifs at enhancers that stay open after stimulation, then measure persistence of chromatin marks and gene expression. Pair these with a bistable feedback model (AP-1 inducing its own enhancers and chromatin remodelers) fitted to the data, to test whether memory requires the positive feedback loop or just an epigenetic mark that AP-1 deposits.
